hero: A tertiary government hospital pediatric ward in Laguna: a 13-year-old Filipino girl with a faint butterfly rash on her cheeks sits up in bed and talks with a pediatric nephrologist who is seated at eye level, while her mother holds her hand; a window shows morning light. Respectful, calm mood, no text.

figures.teaches: The site of immune deposits sets the lupus nephritis class and treatment intensity, and ANCA vasculitis differs by having few deposits.
figures.content: Central glomerular capillary loop cross-section. Labeled deposits: 'Mesangial: class I-II, mild'; 'Subendothelial: class III-IV, proliferation, crescents'; 'Subepithelial: class V, nephrotic'. Side inset 'ANCA vasculitis: neutrophils, necrosis, few deposits'. Bottom strip 'Biopsy class decides treatment; creatinine sets urgency'. Small card 'LN in 50-60% of childhood-onset SLE'.

figures.teaches: Lupus needs a prompt biopsy; ANCA and anti-GBM disease are treated on the clinical picture, with plasma exchange considered by KDIGO criteria.
figures.content: Start 'Child with nephritis + systemic signs'. Three branches by serology: 'ANA, dsDNA, low C3/C4' -> 'Biopsy promptly; hydroxychloroquine; induce by class'; 'ANCA positive' -> 'Do not wait for biopsy; steroids + rituximab (preferred in children)'; 'Anti-GBM positive' -> 'Plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide + steroids now'. Side box 'Consider plasma exchange: creatinine >3.4 mg/dL, dialysis, rapid rise, lung bleeding with hypoxemia'.

card: A teenage girl with a faint butterfly rash talking with a doctor at her hospital bedside while her mother holds her hand.
